title: Measure Zedu cohort retention from week two through day 30
description: Measure repeat usage after a new cohort completes its first-week activation. Define a privacy-conscious retained-cohort measure using aggregate product events, confirm which events exist with the product team, then report the baseline for eligible cohorts over days 8–30 with sample size and data limits. Recommend one retention experiment based on the evidence; do not claim a result before it is measured or contact learners.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Compare day 8-30 retention for cohorts that used Buzz, files or threads in week 1, to find the habit that predicts staying
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Once the retention measure is validated, the most useful next step is knowing which first-week behaviour goes with staying. Approach: with aggregate data only, split eligible cohorts by whether they used each core feature in week 1 (a Buzz call, a shared file, a thread reply), compare their day 8-30 retention with sample sizes, and label the results as correlation, not cause. Done: the comparison table, the caveats, and one onboarding experiment proposal built on the strongest signal.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Validate a privacy-safe day-8-to-30 retention measure before calculating a baseline
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Inventory candidate product events and confirm their meaning and availability before calculating anything. Define cohort eligibility, repeat-usage event, day window, exclusions and minimum reporting threshold; calculate only from permitted aggregate events. Deliver a reproducible metric specification, baseline with sample size and uncertainty where data permit, and a short list of data gaps. Do not export learner-level records, contact learners or claim a result before verification.

upvotes.reason: "Validate a privacy-safe day-8-to-30 retention measure before calculating a baseline" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

pendingIdeas.title: Find the cliff hour by hour: the last action of week one and the first return in week two
pendingIdeas.description: A day-30 number hides the moment people leave. Deliver the two distributions, the three most common last actions, and the one action that most often precedes a return, stated as correlation rather than cause.
